item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Viva Copilot Analytics launches new agent dashboard
item.description:

[Introduction]

We’re introducing the Agent Dashboard, a new dashboard available as part of Copilot Analytics in Microsoft Viva. This dashboard provides visibility into key agent adoption trends and associated Copilot credit usage. It supports insights into agents used within Microsoft 365 Copilot, which may be:

  • Built using Microsoft Copilot Studio, SharePoint, or the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit
  • Built by employees, your organization, Microsoft, or Microsoft partners

This release also enhances the Adoption tab of the Copilot Dashboard, allowing users to view agent insights directly and access the Agent Dashboard for deeper analysis.

[When this will happen:]

  • Public Preview (Worldwide): Begins rolling out in early February 2026 (previously January), expected to complete by mid-February 2026 (previously end of January).
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Begins rolling out in February 2026 (previously late October), expected to complete February 2026 (previously early November).

[How this affects your organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Leaders, delegates, adoption specialists, and administrators using Microsoft Viva Insights
  • Tenants with at least 50 Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses assigned

What will happen:

  • A new Agent Dashboard will be available in Viva Insights under Copilot Analytics
  • Users will find:
    • Key adoption metrics with historical trends (up to 6 months):
      • Number of active agents
      • Number of active agent users
      • Number of agent responses
      • Copilot credits used
      • Number of users using Copilot credits
      • Percentage of Copilot users using agents
    • Screenshot 1: Key adoption metrics with historical trends, including active agents, active users, agent responses, and Copilot credit usage.
    • Monthly and weekly user retention trends, with comparison across groups
  • Screenshot 2: Monthly and weekly user retention trends, with comparison across groups.
    • Top agents based on the following, with the ability to dive deeper into specific agents:
      • Active user count
      • Agent responses
      • Copilot credits consumed
    • Screenshot 3: Agent highlights along with a table of top agents, each with active usage metrics and the ability to dive deeper.
    • Screenshot 4: Individual agent deep dive page with key adoption metrics and trends over time.
  • Minimum group size threshold must be met for agent activity insights.
  • Learn more: Configure manager settings
  • The Adoption tab of the Copilot Dashboard will also include:
    • Contextual insights on how Copilot users are leveraging agents and credits
    • Direct entry points to the Agent Dashboard
  • Screenshot 5: Entry points to the Agent Dashboard from the Copilot Dashboard Adoption tab, including agent usage and Copilot credit usage insights.
  • [What you can do to prepare:]
    • Review and assess the impact for your organization
    • Manage access to the Agent Dashboard using VFAM controls at user, group, and tenant levels (nested under Viva Insights Web app VFAM controls)

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft OneDrive and SharePoint: Generate smart tables of contents for PDFs on the web with Copilot
item.description:
[What and Why:]

We are introducing Smart Table of Contents (Smart TOC) in the Microsoft OneDrive and SharePoint PDF viewer on the web for users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license. When a PDF does not already contain a table of contents, users can ask Copilot to generate a hierarchical, clickable structure that makes it easier to navigate long documents and move between sections. This feature is available only on the web in the initial release and is generated only when a user explicitly requests it.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • Targeted Release (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in early December 2026 and is expected to complete by mid-December 2026.
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in mid-December 2026 and is expected to complete by late December 2026.
  • General Availability (GCC): Rollout will begin in mid-December 2026 and is expected to complete by late December 2026.
  • General Availability (GCC High): Rollout will begin in mid-December 2026 and is expected to complete by late December 2026.
  • General Availability (DoD): Rollout will begin in mid-December 2026 and is expected to complete by late December 2026.

This is a gradual rollout, and not all eligible users will receive the feature at the same time.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

  • Who is affected: Users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license who access PDF files in OneDrive and SharePoint on the web.
  • Platforms/Services: OneDrive, SharePoint, Microsoft 365 Copilot, PDF viewer on the web.

What will happen:

  • The Smart TOC entry point will appear when an eligible user opens a PDF that does not already contain table-of-contents information.
  • The feature is available only in the OneDrive and SharePoint PDF viewer on the web during the initial release.
  • Mobile and desktop applications are not included at this time.
  • Copilot analyzes document structure and generates nested, clickable entries mapped to pages or page ranges.
  • Users with edit permissions can save the generated table of contents into the PDF.
  • The saved table of contents can be displayed by compatible PDF editors.
  • Users with view-only permissions can generate and use Smart TOC for navigation but cannot save the generated table of contents.
  • Smart TOC is available only to users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.
  • AI-generated content may be inaccurate, particularly for scanned or OCR-based PDF files.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No immediate admin action is required.

Before rollout, you may want to:

  • Review Microsoft 365 Copilot license assignments for users who should have access to this capability.
  • Inform eligible users, helpdesk personnel, and support teams about the new PDF navigation experience.
  • Update internal documentation to clarify that saving a generated table of contents requires edit permissions on the PDF.
  • Encourage users to validate AI-generated table-of-contents entries when accuracy is important.

[Compliance considerations:]

  • Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed? Yes. Copilot processes PDF content that the licensed user is already authorized to access in order to generate a table of contents for navigation. Existing file permissions are respected, and saving changes requires edit permissions.
  • Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data? Yes. Copilot analyzes PDF document structure and generates an AI-created hierarchical table of contents. The experience is user-initiated and does not run automatically.
  • Does the change provide end users any new way of interacting with generative AI? Yes. Eligible users can request Copilot to generate a table of contents for PDF files that do not already contain one.
  • Does the change allow a user to enable and disable the feature themselves? Yes. The feature is user-initiated and only runs when a licensed user chooses to generate a Smart TOC.

The experience will clearly indicate that the table of contents was AI generated and may contain inaccuracies.

item.title: [stayInformed] Prompt Column backfill
item.description:
HTML (Needs a final link inserted before shipping):

We are introducing bulk generation of prompt column values for existing Dataverse records. Now, you can have AI-generated values across existing data without requiring record updates to trigger execution.  This feature will reach general availability on November 16, 2026.<br><br><b>How does this affect me?</b><br>When selected, this capability will run asynchronously as a background job and will consume Copilot or AIB credits. Users can monitor and manage the job and view its credit usage in System Jobs.<br><br>Two environment settings in will control this feature:<ul><li><b>Allow bulk processing of existing records</b> will be off by default. It must be enabled to run a bulk job.<li><b>Require review before processing imported prompt columns</b> will be on by default. When enabled, an imported job will be paused for review in System Jobs and can be manually started after review.  Turn this setting off if jobs should start automatically after import.</ul><b>What action do I need to take?</b><br>To use this, go to Power Platform admin center to enable <b>Allow bulk processing of existing records</b> and ensure sufficient <a href="https://aka.ms/feature/21883/1" target="_blank">Copilot</a> or <a href="https://aka.ms/feature/21883/2" target="_blank">AIB</a> credit capacity is available in your environment. Review the <b>Require review before processing imported prompt columns</b> setting to determine whether imported jobs should require review before starting, and make sure to start them promptly after import, if you choose to keep the setting enabled.<br><br> For more information about this capability, please visit <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/maker/data-platform/prompt-column" target="_blank">Prompt columns</a>.  For information about licensing and credits, please visit <a href="https://aka.ms/feature/21883/1" target="_blank">licensing and copilot credits</a> or <a href="https://aka.ms/feature/21883/2" target="_blank">licensing and AIB credits</a>. 

[What and Why:]

Prompt columns can now generate AI values for records that already exist in your table, not just new or updated ones. Makers can choose to apply a prompt to existing records in bulk, optionally filtered to just the rows they need, so historical data gets the same AI-generated insights as incoming data, without touching each record one at a time.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out on early November 2026 and expect to complete by late November 2026.

Public Preview (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out on mid October 2026 and expect to complete by early November 2026.

General Availability (GCC): We will begin rolling out on early November 2026 and expect to complete by late November 2026.

General Availability (GCC High): We will begin rolling out on early November 2026 and expect to complete by late November 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Prompt columns can now generate values for records that already exist in your environment, so you no longer end up with empty prompt column values on historical data. 

Backfill consumes AI credits and runs asynchronously as a background job during maintenance hours. You can monitor and manage the job, and view the credits it consumed in System Jobs. 

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

Two environment settings control this behavior: 

Turn on Allow prompt columns to generate values for existing records to apply a prompt to existing records in an environment. This setting is off by default, so no backfill runs until you enable it. Ensure you have sufficient AI credit capacity in the environment (available under Licensing in Power Platform Admin Center) before you turn this on.  

Require review before processing imported prompt columns holds the backfill job in a paused state when a solution containing prompt columns is imported, so you can review the job before starts. Once your review is complete, start the job from System Jobs. This setting is on by default, turn it off if you'd prefer jobs to start automatically on import. 

When a solution import includes prompt columns with backfill jobs, you'll get a notification (bell icon) letting you know a job needs your attention. Watch for these after a successful import into your target environment. 

[Compliance considerations:]

Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?Yes. The feature uses AI/ML or agent capabilities with Microsoft 365 content, prompts, or service data as described in this message.
Does the change provide end users any new way of interacting with generative AI?Yes. The feature introduces or updates a user-facing AI or Copilot experience as described in this message.
Does the change include an admin control and, can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership?Yes. The feature includes or affects admin controls, policies, permissions, roles, authentication, or management settings as described in this message. Review the linked documentation or admin center controls for group-based configuration support.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft 365 Copilot: new guided Copilot onboarding experience
item.description:
[What and why]

To help organizations increase Microsoft 365 Copilot adoption and build user confidence, we are introducing a new admin-led Copilot onboarding experience for Frontier participants. This guided, in-product experience helps users learn how to use Copilot through role-based activities within the Copilot app. The experience is tailored to the user’s familiarity with Copilot and their license assignment, helping users build confidence through relevant, guided examples while giving organizations control over how onboarding is introduced. This supports Personal and Team Productivity by helping users learn how to use Copilot effectively in their daily work.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Frontier (Worldwide): Rollout begins in late October 2026 and is expected to complete by early November 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Microsoft 365 admins participating in the Frontier program who want to provide guided Copilot onboarding to their users.
  • Users for whom the onboarding experience has been enabled and shared.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft 365 admin center
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot
  • Learning Agent
  • Viva Learning (reporting)

What will happen

  • This is a new, optional onboarding experience that does not change, replace, or retire existing Microsoft 365 Copilot functionality.
  • The experience is disabled by default and must be enabled by an admin with the Global Administrator, Knowledge Administrator, or AI Administrator role. Admins can enable the experience in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Copilot settings > Microsoft 365 Copilot onboarding and include their organization's AI policy as part of the onboarding experience.
  • After enabling onboarding, admins can share the experience with users by using the provided email template or onboarding deep link. When users open the onboarding deep link, the Copilot app launches in the preferred destination set by the admin that shared the experience, such as the Copilot app for Windows, Copilot on the web, or Copilot in Teams.
  • Learning Agent automatically starts the onboarding experience, which takes approximately 5 to 10 minutes to complete, and is personalized based on the user's role, work context, familiarity with Copilot, and license assignment.
  • The Starter journey collects information from the user to personalize the onboarding experience.
  • The Premium journey uses available work and role context to provide relevant examples of how the user can apply Copilot to their work. This journey is only available to users with a Copilot Premium license.
  • If desired, admins with the Global Administrator or Knowledge Administrator role can access and use Viva Learning reporting to review onboarding completion.

Starter journey Copilot onboarding experience

Premium journey Copilot onboarding experience

Microsoft 365 admin center Copilot onboarding flyout menu

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required unless you want to enable Microsoft 365 Copilot onboarding for your organization during the Frontier rollout. If you plan to use the experience:

  • Ensure Learning Agent and Microsoft 365 Copilot are enabled for targeted users who will participate in the onboarding experience.
  • In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot settings > Microsoft 365 Copilot onboarding and enable the experience.
  • Review your organization's AI policy and determine whether you want to include it in the onboarding experience.
  • Share the onboarding experience with users by using the provided email template or onboarding deep link. We recommend that you share the onboarding experience with new or inexperienced users to help them learn how to use Copilot in their role.
  • If you want to view reporting and have the Global Administrator or Knowledge Administrator role, use Viva Learning reporting to review onboarding completion.

[Learn more]

[Compliance considerations]

How does this affect me?
This enhancement introduces column-based security filtering, enabling records to be secured using attribute values rather than traditional record ownership. This allows security admins to define access based on business dimensions such as region or department, making it ideal for scenarios where record ownership does not exist, such as reporting and aggregated datasets. By eliminating the need for artificial ownership or complex sharing models, this approach simplifies security administration, improves scalability, and aligns Dataverse access control more closely with enterprise data governance practices.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Teams admin center device state rules and health alerts retire; use Teams Rooms Pro Management portal
item.description:
Updated October 2, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why:]

As part of the ongoing transition of Teams device management from the Microsoft Teams admin center (TAC) to the Teams Rooms Pro Management portal (PMP), we are retiring device health monitoring capabilities in TAC — specifically the Device state rule (Teams admin center > Notifications & alerts > Rules) and the device health alerts it generates.

Going forward, device health monitoring for all Teams devices (MTR-A, Phones, Panels etc.) is delivered through the Teams Rooms Pro Management portal, which provides device health signals, monitoring, and incident management in a single unified portal. This is a continuation of the change previously communicated in MC1227622, where Android device management capabilities including inventory, updates, health monitoring, and settings transitioned from TAC to PMP.

[Rollout schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide, GCC): We will begin rolling out late October 2026 (previously late September) and expect to complete by late October 2026 (previously late September).

[Impact on your organization:]

Who is affected: 

  1. Admins who currently use the Device state rule in the Teams admin center to monitor Teams device health, and anyone who receives the resulting offline-device alerts in Teams or via webhook.

What will happen:

  1. The Device state rule page under Notifications & alerts > Rules in the Teams admin center will no longer be available, and existing rule configurations will stop being evaluated.
  2. Device offline / health alerts will stop being delivered to the Admin Alerts and Notifications team's MonitoringAlerts channel.
  3. Any webhook integrations configured against the Device state rule will stop receiving the alert payload. 
  4. Existing rule configurations and historical alerts in TAC will not be migrated to the Pro Management portal.

What replaces it:

  1. Device health signals, monitoring, and incident management are available for all Teams device types in the Teams Rooms Pro Management portal, with alerting and notification configured in the portal. There is no change to the health data collected from devices — only to where it is surfaced and how alerts needs to be configured by admins.

There is no change to end users. This affects admin monitoring workflows only.

[Action required / Recommendations:]

  1. Review your existing Device state rule configuration in the Teams admin center (Notifications & alerts > Rules > Device state rule) and record which devices and device users are currently monitored.
  2. Identify any webhook integrations. If you send the Device state rule payload to an external system (ITSM, ticketing, monitoring dashboard, custom workflow), plan the equivalent integration from the Pro Management portal before the retirement date.
  3. Set up health monitoring and alert notifications in the Pro Management portal for your device fleet, and validate you're receiving alerts for same.
  4. Monitor the transition article for feature-specific updates and timelines: Transitioning Teams Android Device Management from Teams Admin Center to the Teams Rooms Pro Management Portal

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified; review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Dynamics 365 Contact Center - Use role-based enforcement for recording and transcription downloads
item.description:
We are announcing the ability to use role-based enforcement for recording and transcription downloads in Dynamics 365 Contact Center. This feature will reach general availability on October 31, 2026.

How does this affect me?
This feature helps organizations better protect sensitive customer communications by separating permissions to view recordings and transcripts from permissions to download them. Admins can assign new Dataverse security roles to prevent selected users from downloading recordings or transcripts while still allowing them to view and play back content as permitted by existing access.

The two new Dataverse security roles that will be available are:
  • Deny Recording Download
  • Deny Transcription Download
When either role is assigned to a user:
  • The user can continue to view and play back recordings and transcripts as permitted by existing access.
  • The user is blocked from downloading the corresponding artifact.
Enforcement of these models is applied server-side across the Dynamics 365 Contact Center UI, public and internal APIs, and direct download URLs or integrations. Download requests will also be denied regardless of how they are initiated.

Access control is driven entirely by Dataverse role assignment. The deny roles override implicit download behavior without affecting recording, transcription, or playback functionality.

These controls help reduce the risk of unauthorized data export, support compliance and data governance requirements, and allow organizations to maintain operational visibility without allowing data removal.

What action do I need to take?
This message is for awareness, and no action is required.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Exchange Online: Exchange Web Services (EWS) enforcement update for EWSAllowedAppIDs
item.description:
[What and why]

As previously communicated in MC1466860 and MC1447678, Microsoft is continuing the retirement of Exchange Web Services (EWS) in Exchange Online.

Beginning October 10, 2026, setting EWSEnabled=True will no longer be sufficient to allow EWS access for affected Worldwide tenants. Organizations that require EWS must configure EWSAllowedAppIDs to specify which applications are permitted to access EWS.

This change is part of the final phase of EWS retirement and is intended to help organizations identify EWS dependencies, reduce service disruption, and support migration planning.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD: Beginning in early October 2026 and expected to complete by early July 2027

Key milestones for Worldwide tenants with EWSEnabled=True and no configured EWSAllowedAppIDs list:

DateMilestone
October 2, 2026Microsoft identifies affected Worldwide tenants. After this date, tenants that enable EWS must configure EWSAllowedAppIDs themselves.
October 8-9, 2026Microsoft creates and populates EWSAllowedAppIDs for qualifying Worldwide tenants based on EWS activity observed during the previous 60 days.
October 10, 2026EWSAllowedAPPIDs becomes required when EWSEnabled=True. Applications note included in the allow list may lose access to EWS.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Exchange Online administrators
  • Organizations that continue to use applications or services that depend on EWS
  • Tenants with EWSEnabled=True

Platforms and services

  • Exchange Online
  • Exchange Web Services (EWS)

What will happen

  • Beginning October 10, 2026, affected Worldwide tenants with EWSEnabled=True must have a configured EWSAllowedAppIDs allow list. Applications not included in the allow list may lose access to EWS.
  • For identified Worldwide tenants with EWSEnabled=True and no configured EWSAllowedAppIDs list on October 3 2026, Microsoft creates and populates an allow list using EWS activity observed during the previous 60 days. Infrequently used applications may not be identified.
  • Cross-tenant organization relationships are not affected by the EWSAllowedAppIDs requirement.
  • Organizations remain responsible for reviewing, validating, and maintaining EWSAllowedAppIDs.
  • EWSAllowedAppIDs is a replacement list. Ensure all required AppIDs are included whenever the configuration is updated.
  • Microsoft applications and scenarios that may generate EWS traffic include Outlook for Windows, Classic Outlook for Mac, Excel Power Query, Power BI, and Exchange Server hybrid scenarios.
  • Outlook for Windows customers should be on August 2026 build 16.0.20430.20092 or later. If EWS-related issues continue after disabling EWS, the cause may be customer-forced configuration. Test whether blocking EWS for the Office client AppID is possible without impact.
  • New Outlook for Mac is not affected. If your organization continues to use Classic Outlook for Mac, ensure the Microsoft Office AppID is included in EWSAllowedAppIDs.
  • Tenants with EWSEnabled not configured (Null) remain subject to Microsoft's phased EWS retirement process and will have EWS disabled as part of that rollout.
  • Organizations with EWSEnabled=True and a configured EWSAllowedAppIDs allow list will not have their EWSEnabled setting modified by Microsoft before April 2027.

[Action required and recommendations]

If your organization relies on EWS:

  • Review EWS usage reports and identify applications and services that require continued EWS access.
  • Configure and validate an EWSAllowedAppIDs allow list before October 10, 2026.
  • Include Microsoft first-party applications that continue to rely on EWS if they appear in your usage reporting.
  • Ensure all required AppIDs are included whenever EWSAllowedAppIDs is updated.
  • Keep the allow list current as applications are added, removed, or migrated away from EWS.
  • Enable EWS only when required for approved applications.
  • Continue planning migration from EWS to Microsoft Graph where possible.

To verify the configured allow list: Get-OrganizationConfig -RetrieveEwsOperationAccessPolicy | Format-List EwsAllowedAppIDs

Allow up to 24 hours for EWSAllowedAppIDs changes to take effect and approximately one hour for EWSEnabled changes.

Important: EWSAllowList is unrelated to EWS retirement and does not replace EWSAllowedAppIDs.

Learn more

  • Exchange Online EWS, Your Time is Almost Up | Microsoft Community Hub
  • How to revert the Outlook Desktop WebView based Room Finder to the legacy Room Finder | Microsoft Support
  • Impact of Exchange Online EWS Deprecation on Hybrid Rich Coexistence and Cross-org Sharing | Microsoft Community Hub
  • Notes from the field: testing EWSAllowedAppIDs safely | Microsoft Community Hub

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does this change include an admin control?Yes. EWSAllowedAppIDs introduces a tenant-level administrative control that allows Exchange Online administrators to explicitly define which applications are permitted to access EWS.
Does this change alter how existing customer data is accessed?Yes. The change modifies how applications are authorized to access Exchange Online data through EWS by requiring administrators to explicitly allow approved application IDs as retirement enforcement begins.
Does this change alter how admins monitor, manage, or demonstrate compliance-related activities?Yes. Administrators must identify EWS dependencies, configure and maintain an EWSAllowedAppIDs allow list, and validate application access as part of preparing for EWS retirement.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Viva Engage: Community feeds improvements
item.description:
Updated October 1, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[Introduction:]

We’re introducing a simpler way to view conversations in Viva Engage communities, organized by recent posts rather than recent activity. This new view is designed to make it easier for users to follow discussions and will be available as an option, alongside the current system, for those who prefer sorting by recent activity and filtering to new conversations only.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 513275.

[When this will happen:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in October 2026 (previously September).

[How this will affect your organization:]

This change should align better with how people expect to browse and engage with content in their communities, while still preserving the triage flow for those who prefer it.

Who is affected: All Viva Engage users in your organization.

Current experience:

  • Communities default to “new” and “recent activity” if there’s any new content (posts or replies).
  • If there’s no new content, the feed falls back to “all.”
  • Unread indicators on content only exist in the “new” feed.

New experience:

  • The feature will be ON by default.
  • Communities will default to “all” and “recent posts”:

  • Unread indicators will exist in both the “new” and “all” feeds.
  • A sticky user preference will be introduced:
    • If someone changes the feed (new/all) or sort order (recent posts/recent activity), we will maintain that setting across their communities.
    • If someone picks “new” and there’s no new content in the next community, we will fall back to “all” for that community visit, but “new” will remain the preference for that user.

[What you can do to prepare:]

No action is required.

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate

item.title: [stayInformed] Upgraded call history in Teams Calls app

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Entra App Gallery: Self-service onboarding for new applications
item.description:
[What and why]

We are introducing a self-service onboarding experience for new applications submitted to the Microsoft Entra App Gallery. This experience helps independent software vendors (ISVs) validate supported single sign-on (SSO) and user provisioning integrations before submission, identify and resolve common configuration issues earlier in the process, and track submission status through a guided workflow in the Microsoft Entra admin center. By enabling publishers to validate integrations and manage submissions directly, this experience streamlines the publishing process.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Public Preview: Available now
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in mid-November 2026 and expected to complete by late December 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Independent software vendors (ISVs) and developers submitting new applications to the Microsoft Entra App Gallery
  • Administrators responsible for publishing applications to the Microsoft Entra App Gallery

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Entra admin center
  • Microsoft Entra App Gallery

What will happen

  • Publishers can validate supported OpenID Connect (OIDC), SAML, and user provisioning integrations before application submission.
  • Publishers can create and manage App Gallery submissions through a guided workflow in the Microsoft Entra admin center.
  • Validation results can be associated with application submissions.
  • Publishers can provide required application information and supporting documentation during onboarding.
  • Applications can be submitted directly to Microsoft for review.
  • Publishers can track submission status and respond to reviewer feedback.
  • Public Preview currently supports new Microsoft Entra App Gallery application submissions only.
  • Existing applications already published in the Microsoft Entra App Gallery will continue to use the current update and removal process.
  • No impact is expected for organizations that do not publish applications to the Microsoft Entra App Gallery.
  • This experience does not change how users access applications.

[Action Required and recommendations]

No action is required.

Organizations that publish applications to the Microsoft Entra App Gallery should review the new onboarding experience and prepare application publishing teams for the updated submission workflow.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Retirement of SharePoint One-Time Passcode (SPO OTP) and transition to Microsoft Entra B2B
item.description:
Updated October 1, 2026: Phase 1, which enables Entra B2B for new external sharing, is now fully rolled out for Production environments. To ensure a smooth transition, Phase 2, the retirement of SharePoint Online OTP, has been rescheduled to begin in mid-October 2026 and is expected to complete by end of November 2026 for Production environments.

Both Phase 1 and Phase 2 roll outs exclude GCC, GCCH & DoD. New dates for these environments will be communicated via Message center when we are ready to proceed. Thank you for your patience.

[Introduction]

We are retiring SharePoint One‑Time Passcode (SPO OTP) authentication in OneDrive and SharePoint starting mid-October 2026. Beginning in May 2026, new external sharing invitations and authentication will start using Microsoft Entra B2B instead of SPO OTP. This transition simplifies external collaboration, aligns authentication with Microsoft identity standards, and enables consistent guest lifecycle management, governance, and Conditional Access coverage across Microsoft 365.

[When this will happen]

  • May & June 2026: Invitation and authentication for new external sharing transitions to Microsoft Entra B2B. Users who previously authenticated via SPO OTP will continue to have access to specific people links even without a B2B guest account yet.
  • Mid-October 2026: Retirement of SPO OTP authentication begins. External users without a guest account get access denied on previously shared specific people links. To restore access, a guest account must be created in Entra B2B, or an allowed user must share/re-share at least one file/folder/site.
  • Retirement is expected to complete by end of November 2026.

[How this affects your organization]

Who is affected

  • All Microsoft 365 tenants (commercial, government, sovereign).
  • All external users who access OneDrive or SharePoint files, folders, or sites.

What will happen

  • The EnableAzureADB2BIntegration setting will no longer control external sharing behavior beginning May 2026.
  • SPO OTP authentication will retire beginning mid-October 2026.
  • The option to disable Entra B2B integration will be removed.

Impact on external users

  • External users who already have an Entra B2B guest account in your directory:
    • No change in behavior.
  • External users without a B2B guest account:
    • Specific people links shared after changes rolled out to your tenant: A guest account will be automatically created via the Entra B2B Invitation Manager and authentication will use Entra B2B. The email one-time passcode feature is now turned on by default for all new tenants and for any existing tenants where you haven’t explicitly turned it off. Please refer to this article to learn more.
    • Specific people links shared before changes rolled out to your tenant: SPO OTP authentication continues until the retirement reaches the tenant. After the retirement, these users will receive access denied until a matching B2B guest account exists.

Restoring access after retirement

  • Admins can manually create a guest account for the external user at any time. Alternatively, an internal user with permissions needs to share or re-share at least one file, folder, or site, which will automatically create the guest account and restore access to all previously shared content.

[What you need to do to prepare]

To ensure a smooth transition:

  • Review external sharing policies and conditional access settings for guests in SharePoint and Entra admin centers.
  • Ensure that Microsoft Entra is configured to allow guest invitations for the appropriate users. For example, assign the Guest Inviter role to users who need external sharing or are responsible for creating guest accounts.
  • Inform users that, beginning in mid-October 2026, some external collaborators may see an access denied message when opening older links that were previously authenticated with SharePoint Online OTP. This can occur if a matching B2B guest account was not created for the email address used with the original sharing link.
    • To restore access, users can share or reshare at least one file with the external collaborator. This creates the required B2B guest account, after which the collaborator can continue accessing previously shared links.
  • If your organization relies on email OTP authentication via Entra, ensure it is not disabled in Entra External ID settings. See Email OTP for B2B guests.
  • Optionally, identify external collaborators without guest accounts via external sharing reports. Proactively create guest accounts to retain access.
  • Update internal documentation.

Learn more:

  • Add and manage B2B collaboration users in the Microsoft Entra admin center | External ID | Microsoft Entra | Microsoft Learn
  • Email one-time passcode authentication for B2B guest users | External ID | Microsoft Entra | Microsoft Learn
  • Frequently Asked Questions: Improvements to external sharing in OneDrive & SharePoint | SharePoint in Microsoft 365 | Microsoft Learn
  • Overview: B2B collaboration with external guests for your workforce | External ID | Microsoft Entra | Microsoft Learn
  • Quickstart: Add a guest user and send an invitation | External ID | Microsoft Entra | Microsoft Learn
  • SharePoint and OneDrive integration with Microsoft Entra B2B | SharePoint in Microsoft 365 | Microsoft Learn
  • Configure external collaboration - Microsoft Entra External ID | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

Compliance QuestionAnswer
Does the change alter how existing customer data is accessed, processed, or stored?Yes. This change retires SPO OTP authentication and requires all external users to authenticate using Microsoft Entra B2B guest accounts, which alters the authentication method used to access existing SharePoint and OneDrive content.
Does the change modify Conditional Access policies or enforcement?Yes. After retirement, all external users will authenticate through Entra B2B and become fully subject to Microsoft Entra Conditional Access, Identity Protection, and guest governance policies.
Does the change provide a new way of communicating between users, tenants, or subscriptions?Yes. External sharing invitations will be routed through Microsoft Entra B2B Invitation Manager instead of SharePoint’s OTP invitation flow.
Does the change alter how admins monitor, report on, or demonstrate compliance activities?Yes. Authentication events and guest lifecycle actions will be logged through Entra audit logs rather than SPO OTP logs, changing where admins review authentication and guest access activity.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft 365: The Next Generation of File & Folder Sharing
item.description:
Updated October 1, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why:]

We're introducing the third-generation Microsoft 365 sharing experience to make collaboration simpler, smarter, and more secure by default. At the center of this update is a new hero link—a single sharing link that controls access to a file or folder.

Users will see one consistent sharing experience whether they copy a link, share through email, or use the browser URL. The hero link consolidates sharing controls into a single link that can be updated after it has been shared, reducing the need to create and resend new links when access requirements change.

[Rollout schedule:]

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Rolling out early October 2026 (previously mid-September) through late October 2026

[Impact on your organization:]

Who is affected: All users who share or manage files and folders in Microsoft 365.

Platforms and services: SharePoint, OneDrive, and Microsoft 365 file-sharing experiences.

What will happen:

  • Every file and folder will have a single primary sharing link, called the hero link, displayed in the sharing dialog.
  • The hero link settings determine who can access the item beyond people who are explicitly granted access.
  • Adding people directly to a file or folder remains unchanged and continues to be the simplest way to share content.

Screenshot - Add people screen when sharing 

  • By default, the hero link is set to Only people added to the file, meaning the link itself does not grant access to anyone.

Screenshot - Share file view with hero link

  • Users can broaden access to people in the organization with the link or, where permitted by organizational policy, to anyone with the link.
  • Users can choose whether recipients can view, edit, or view without downloading, depending on available permissions.
  • Changing the audience for the hero link updates the existing link rather than creating a new one.
  • If recipients cannot open a previously shared file, the sender can expand access on the same hero link without redistributing a new URL.
  • Existing sharing links will continue to function and will appear under Other links in the sharing dialog.
  • Effective access remains the most permissive combination of direct permissions, inherited permissions, group-based permissions, and link-based permissions.
  • Users will see a tutorial experience upon opening the new share dialog for the first time.

[Action required/Recommendations:]

No action is required before rollout.

Organizations should consider the following preparation activities:

  • Review internal sharing guidance and end-user documentation to reflect the new single-link sharing model.
  • Communicate the updated sharing experience to users who regularly collaborate across teams and organizations.
  • Evaluate site-level default sharing settings where different sharing behaviors are required.

Learn more:

  • Walkthrough Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3RpE0KrQmcA&t=4s
  • Announcement Blog: https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/onedriveblog/simple-smart-and-secure-the-next-step-in-sharing-files-in-microsoft-365/4411655

Admin controls

  • Administrators can configure the default audience for the hero link at the SharePoint site collection or OneDrive level by using the DefaultMainLinkScope parameter in SharePoint PowerShell.
  • Supported values are:
    • OnlyPeopleAdded (default)
    • Organization
  • There is currently no tenant-wide equivalent setting for the hero link audience.
  • DefaultMainLinkScope controls only the default audience and does not prevent users from broadening access when allowed by policy.
  • Hero links start with view permissions by default.
  • Existing default sharing link settings and link expiration policies continue to apply to legacy links and do not govern hero links.

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: Improved file sharing experience in external chats
item.description:
Updated October 1, 2026: We have updated the content. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

We’re improving the file-sharing experience in Microsoft Teams external (federated) chats by making the Attach file (paperclip) and drag-and-drop experiences available by default. This change only impacts tenants who have not adjusted the policy that controls file attachment in an external Teams chat. To opt out of this change, disable the capability using the Teams PowerShell setting provided in the “Action required and recommendations” section below. This can be done before the rollout and your policy setting will be respected. This update does not change your OneDrive or SharePoint external-sharing settings or override existing access restrictions. 

Prior to this change, when existing OneDrive and SharePoint policies allow, users can already share files in external chats by sharing a link to the file. This update makes that flow easier by adding the Attach file (paperclip) and drag-and-drop experiences directly in Teams. Files uploaded from the user’s device are stored in the sender’s OneDrive, while cloud files remain stored in their existing location. Teams then assigns permissions to chat participants, subject to existing OneDrive and SharePoint sharing policies. Senders can still review, modify, or remove file access before sending the message. This reduces the need to assign permissions manually, while allowing senders to stay in control.

  • More info: Share files and Loop in external chats - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn

[Rollout schedule]

  • Targeted Release: Beginning in late October 2026 and expected to complete by late November 2026
  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Beginning in late October 2026 and expected to complete by late November 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Microsoft Teams external access (federation)
  • This change applies only to organizations where the setting has not been explicitly configured. Any customers who have left the configuration in the default state will be impacted. 
  • Users participating in external 1:1 chats, external group chats, and meeting chats

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams
  • External (federated) 1:1 chats
  • External (federated) group chats
  • Meeting chats
  • Teams desktop app
  • Teams web app

What will happen

  • The ability for users to attach and share files in external chats will be enabled for all Microsoft 365 tenants, unless your organization has previously explicitly disabled this setting in Teams. Any customers who have left the configuration in the default state will be impacted.
  • Users can already paste file links into external chants. This ability is unchanged. With this change, users will also have the ability to attach and share files using the paperclip option or drag and drop in external (federated) chats.
  • Files shared through these experiences continue to be stored and shared through OneDrive or SharePoint. Files uploaded from a user’s device are stored in the sender’s OneDrive, while existing cloud files remain in their current location. 
  • Organizations that want the Teams attachment experience in external chats to remain disabled must reapply the disabled setting after rollout.
  • When automatic permission assignment is enabled, Teams assigns permissions to participants in the external chat for files uploaded using paperclip or drag-and-drop, subject to existing OneDrive and SharePoint policies.
  • Senders can review, modify, or remove sharing permissions before sending a file.
  • Senders can continue to modify or revoke access after a file has been shared.
  • Automatic permission assignment applies only to files shared through the paperclip or drag-and-drop experience.
  • The files will be shared as hyperlinks after send. 
  • Existing OneDrive and SharePoint sharing controls continue to govern access.
  • Existing sensitivity labels, domain restrictions, and security protections continue to apply.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required to preserve external-sharing restrictions already configured in OneDrive and SharePoint; this update does not change those restrictions. To review or change these controls, see Manage sharing settings for SharePoint and OneDrive in Microsoft 365. 

[To disable file attachments in external chats]

To opt out of this change, apply the following Teams PowerShell setting if you have not already explicitly configured this setting:

Set-CsTeamsFilesPolicy -Identity Global -FileSharingInChatsWithExternalUsers Disabled

Verify the setting:

Get-CsTeamsFilesPolicy | Select Identity, FileSharingInChatsWithExternalUsers

Recommended actions:

  • Review your SharePoint, OneDrive, and Microsoft Entra external sharing configuration because these settings continue to govern what external recipients can access.
  • Inform helpdesk and support teams about the updated attachment experience and the distinction between Teams attachment controls and OneDrive/SharePoint access controls. 
  • Update user training and internal documentation as needed.
  • Communicate to users that:
    • They can attach files directly in chats with people outside the organization.
    • When automatic permission assignment is enabled, Teams assigns chat participants access to files shared via paperclip icon, subject to existing OneDrive and SharePoint policies. Senders can review, modify, or remove access before sending.
    • Pasted file links retain their existing permissions.
    • Files uploaded to external chats are stored in the sender's OneDrive and display.

Optional configuration to allow attachments without automatic permission assignment:

To disable automatic permission assignment while continuing to allow file attachments in external chats:

Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy -Identity Global -AutoShareFilesInExternalChats Disabled

If automatic permission assignment is disabled, users may need to manually grant access to shared files before external recipients can open them.

Allow several hours for policy changes to propagate before users see the updated experience.

Learn more:

  • Share files and Loop in external chats - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. Uploaded files shared through Attach or drag-and-drop can automatically receive permissions for participants in external chats. Existing OneDrive and SharePoint controls continue to govern access. Uploaded files are stored in the sender’s OneDrive.
Does the change provide a new way of communicating between users, tenants, or subscriptions?Yes. The direct file-attachment experience in external (federated) chats becomes available by default; the existing ability to paste file links remains unchanged.
Does the change include an admin control, and can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership?Yes. Admins can separately control Teams file attachments and automatic permission assignment through Teams PowerShell policies. OneDrive and SharePoint sharing settings continue to govern external file access.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Unified management of app and agent availability and installation in Teams, Outlook, and the Microsoft 365 app
item.description:
Updated October 1, 2026: We have updated the content and timeline. Thank you for your patience.

What it is

Microsoft is rolling out a new feature to streamline how app and agent availability and installation is managed across Teams, Outlook, and Microsoft 365 Copilot. Until now, IT admins configured availability and installation settings separately in both the Microsoft 365 Admin Center (MAC) and the Teams Admin Center (TAC), which led to mismatches. With this update, you’ll be able to unify availability and installation policies for apps and agents across both portals, making app management more consistent and efficient.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 393931, 485712 and 503105.

When this will happen: 

  • App and agent AVAILABILITY unification (section A): Rollout began in late September 2025. The Phase 3 timeline will be announced separately, at least 60 days before that phase begins.
  • App and agent INSTALLATION unification (section B): Rollout begins at the end of September 2026. 

A: Unify app availability across admin centers

1. Phase 1 – Default Tenant Unification of App/Agent Availability

We will begin rolling out this feature at the end of September 2025. This initial phase targets tenants that have never modified their organization-wide defaults, app availability, or block/unblock in either the Microsoft 365 admin center or the Teams admin center. At the end of this phase, agent and app manageability will be unified across both Microsoft 365 admin center and Teams admin center ensuring agent and Microsoft 365 apps availability policies are in alignment for all future administrative changes. This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 393931.

2.Phase 2 – Modified Tenants Unification of App/Agent Availability

This phase targets tenants that have previously modified their organization-wide defaults, app availability, or block/unblock settings in either admin center. These tenants will be transitioned to a unified management experience across both Microsoft 365 and Teams admin centers.

  • For tenants with no agent or app availability differences across both admin centers, guidance will be provided to help maintain unified availability policy for all future changes.

For tenants with agent or app availability differences across both admin centers, a wizard in the Teams admin center will help identify affected agents and apps and guide through resolving discrepancies.

  • As part of this phase we will also enable administrators to manage Microsoft 365 certified SaaS applications within their tenant through org-wide settings for third-party apps. This has been rolled out completely for all tenants.
  • This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 485712 & 503105.

This phase has been fully rolled out to all tenants. Tenants can choose to align through the wizard experience available in Teams admin center.

Note: In this phase, no changes will be applied to org-wide settings or app-level settings without administrator action.

3. Phase 3 – Automatic Unification (Future)

Tenants that have not taken action to unify availability through the wizard experience released in Phase 1 and Phase 2 will have their availability automatically unified across MAC and TAC as part of this phase. We will inform customers of the timeline and additional details at least 60 days in advance before this phase begins.

B: Unified app and agent installation management 

This capability unifies installation management across the Teams admin center and Microsoft 365 admin center. Administrators can manage supported app and agent installations from either portal, with changes synchronized across both admin centers. 

Who receives this capability? 

Tenants whose app and agent availability has been unified through any of the phases described in section A are eligible. Once rollout begins, this capability will be automatically enabled for tenants whose availability is already unified as part of Section A. Tenants that unify their availability later will receive this capability automatically once unified. 

Note: This capability is separate from availability unification described in section A . It does not automatically unify app or agent availability. 

When will it roll out? 

Rollout will begin at the end of September 2026 for eligible tenants. This date applies only to installation management (section B). 

Is administrator action required? 

No additional action is required to enable installation unification for eligible tenants. Existing installation assignments for supported apps and agents will be synchronized across both admin centers. 

Important: App installation is no longer managed through Teams app setup policies. Installations previously made through those policies are not unified as part of this change.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Transitioning Teams Android Device Management from Teams admin Center to the Teams Rooms Pro Management portal
item.description:
Updated October 1, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[Introduction]

As part of our ongoing mission to deliver a modern, secure, and scalable one-stop management portal for admins, we are transitioning Teams Android device management from the Teams admin center (TAC) to the Teams Rooms Pro Management portal (PMP).

This move consolidates management of all Teams devices, including Teams Rooms on Windows, Teams Rooms on Android, Teams phones, and Teams panels, into a single unified portal, providing IT admins a consistent and seamless experience for managing devices at scale.

This message is associated with Roadmap ID 555235.

[When this will happen:]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Effective July 2, 2026, the rollout is 100% complete across all regions in the Public cloud.
  • General Availability (GCC High): We expect to start the rollout by mid-August 2026 and complete by late-August 2026 (previously late-July).
  • General Availability (GCC and DoD): We expect to complete the rollout by mid-October 2026 (previously late-August).
  • Device management deprecation in TAC: The deprecation of Teams device management capabilities in TAC will begin in October 2026 and will roll out in phases based on device type and feature readiness.

[How this affects your organization:]

Who is affected:

Admins who manage Teams Rooms on Android, Teams phones, Teams panels, and SIP Phones.

What will happen:

  • By end of June 2026, Android device management capabilities, including inventory, updates, health monitoring, and settings will transition from TAC to PMP for the device types, Teams Rooms on Android, Teams phones, Teams panels and SIP Phones.
  • The following capabilities will be available and enhanced in PMP:
    • Device inventories for Android-based Teams Rooms, phones, and panels, including metadata and app information
    • Remote device actions (restart, log collection, sign-in/out, provisioning, and more)
    • Update management
    • Device settings management
    • Device health monitoring
    • SIP device management
  • PMP will become the primary portal for all Teams device management. By November 2026, overlapping TAC capabilities (updates, settings, restart, sign-in/out, log collection, provisioning) will be deprecated in TAC.
  • The article below serves as the main information source for this transition. It has been updated with the latest timelines, milestones, migration guidance, and readiness steps. We will keep updating it as the rollout progresses.
    • Transitioning Teams Android Device Management from Teams Admin Center to the Teams Rooms Pro Management Portal - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn

[What you need to do to prepare:]

  • Monitor the below article for any feature specific updates and timelines. This article also provides migration guidance and pre-requisites for successful transition to PMP.
    • Transitioning Teams Android Device Management from Teams Admin Center to the Teams Rooms Pro Management Portal - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn
  • Learn more about Pro Management portal features with these Teams Rooms Pro Management short YouTube videos.
  • Update internal helpdesk and IT documentation to reference PMP as the new management portal.

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Simplifying AI access: Introducing usage-based billing
item.description:
Updated October 1, 2026: We have updated the content and timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

The new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business combines everyday AI via user subscription license with Advanced AI via usage-based billing. We are now making it easier to access eligible usage-based AI experiences, including Copilot Cowork and other long-running, autonomous agentic capabilities, when you purchase Microsoft 365 Copilot Business. Usage-based billing will be included by default with eligible new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business purchases, reducing billing complexity while giving your organization flexibility to expand usage over time based on business needs.

You have been identified as a customer who may be affected by this change.

What is changing

  • With eligible new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business purchases, pay-as-you-go usage-based billing will be configured by default to provide access to eligible usage-based experiences with less billing setup. Microsoft will automatically create the required Azure resources and apply a spending policy that enables usage-based billing including default spending limits and future eligible services. 
  • For existing Microsoft 365 Copilot customers, purchasing a new Copilot Business seat will deploy usage-based billing across all Microsoft 365 Copilot subscriptions in your tenant. 
  • The resulting spending policy will have a spending limit of 4,000 Copilot credits per user per month with charges based on actual usage.
  • Charges apply only when these experiences are used, subject to the usage controls and spending limits established by your administrator.
  • We will begin rolling out this change to eligible customers in supported markets. The change will not initially be available in Australia, Belgium, Brazil, France, Germany, India, Italy, Korea, Netherlands, Poland, Spain. We will provide additional information about availability in these markets when available. 

What is not changing

  • Your existing Microsoft 365 Copilot Business subscription benefits and payment terms do not change.
  • Capabilities already included with your license remain included; this change adds a spending policy for eligible usage-based experiences.
  • If your organization already has a spending policy configured, the existing spending policy remains in place.

When this will happen

  • Starting October 19, 2026: The change applies to eligible new purchases made directly from Microsoft, including through Microsoft web and the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • Starting December 1, 2026: The change applies to eligible new purchases made through Cloud Solution Provider (CSP) channels.

How usage-based billing works

  • If your organization does not already have the required pay-as-you-go Azure resource and/or spending policy, it will be created as part of the eligible purchase and product setup.
  • Administrators can review and manage usage controls and spending policy in Cost Management in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • Your organization can adjust its spending policies and controls to align with its needs. Disabling usage-based billing prevents access to experiences that require it.

What you can do to prepare

  • Review which eligible usage-based experiences—including Copilot Cowork and other long-running, autonomous agentic capabilities—may support your organization’s needs.
  • Review your organization’s usage-based billing, governance, and cost-management requirements.
  • On or after the applicable date, confirm or adjust usage controls and spending policies in the Microsoft 365 admin center. 

Learn more

  • Cost Management in the Microsoft 365 admin center: https://admin.cloud.microsoft/#/copilot/costmanagement/overview
  • Usage-based billing and cost management for Copilot Credits: learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/usage-based-billing-overview-copilot-credits
  • Cloud Based Billing: What is a cloud subscription? - Microsoft Cost Management | Microsoft Learn

item.title: [stayInformed] Dynamics 365 Contact Center - Use after conversation presence status for wrap-up activities
item.description:
We are announcing the ability to use after conversation presence status for wrap-up activities in Dynamics 365 Contact Center. This feature will reach general availability on October 30, 2026.

How does this affect me?
This feature disambiguates the Busy/DND presence state of a representative by letting the supervisor clearly distinguish agents performing after-conversation wrap-up work from representatives who are generally Busy or in DND, reducing operational ambiguity.

After conversation work presence (ACW) introduces dedicated, system-driven presence states like Busy - After Conversation Work or DND - After Conversation Work, to indicate the post-conversation wrapping-up state of the customer service representatives.

These states are automatically applied to a representative by the system when they are wrapping up the conversation, depending on how the administrator has configured the wrap-up experience in the admin center. The presence status is set by the system and is visually distinct from other manually set or system evaluated Busy/DND presence states.

What action do I need to take?
This message is for awareness, and no action is required.

item.title: [stayInformed] Power Automate - Enable Process Intelligence Studio in object-centric process mining
item.description:
We are announcing the availability of Process Intelligence Studio in object-centric process mining in Power Automate Process Mining. This feature will reach general availability on October 31, 2026.

How does this affect me?
Process Intelligence Studio makes process analysis easier and more intuitive. It gives teams one place to explore data, compare scenarios, and uncover insights faster—without jumping between tools. item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Viva Engage: Email updates for frontline users without an active Exchange mailbox
item.description:
Updated September 30, 2026: We have updated the content timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[Introduction]

Viva Engage will stop sending email notifications to users who do not have a valid mailbox or routable email destination. Previously, email notifications could still be attempted for these users, resulting in repeated delivery retries, increased load on email systems, and, in some cases, delays to important business communications.

This change reduces unnecessary email traffic, improves delivery efficiency, and helps ensure important communications are delivered reliably and on time.

Users with supported mailbox configurations, including cloud mailboxes, on-premises mailboxes, shared mailboxes, and other routable email destinations, will continue to receive Viva Engage email notifications as expected.

Notifications delivered through supported channels such as Microsoft Teams remain unaffected.

[When this will happen:]

General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout begins mid-October 2026 (previously end of September) and is expected to complete by end of December 2026 (previously end of October).

[How this affects your organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Users who do not have a valid mailbox or routable email destination.
  • Microsoft 365 admins managing Viva Engage users and mailbox configurations.

What will happen:

  • Viva Engage will no longer attempt to send email notifications to users who do not have a valid mailbox or routable email destination.
  • Users with cloud, on-premises, shared, or other supported mailbox configurations will continue to receive email notifications as expected.
  • This change does not affect the existing email notification experience for users with a valid mailbox or routable email destination.
  • Notifications delivered through Microsoft Teams or other supported channels are not impacted.
  • The change is enabled by default and applies automatically.
  • Organizations may see:
    • Reduced load on email systems and gateways.
    • Fewer retry attempts for undeliverable messages.
    • Improved email delivery efficiency and reliability.

[What you can do to prepare:]

  • No action is required.
  • Review your Exchange Online licensing configuration to identify users without mailbox access.
  • Evaluate your notification strategy (e.g., Teams vs. Email) for frontline workers.
  • Inform helpdesk and user support teams of the expected behavior change.
  • Update internal documentation if email notifications are referenced for frontline users.

[Compliance considerations:]

  • Alters how existing customer data is processed: Email notifications to users without mailboxes are no longer attempted, reducing unnecessary processing of undeliverable messages.
  • No other compliance impacts identified.

The change gives administrators clearer visibility into storage use, advance notice of potential restrictions, and several ways to remain within capacity, including removing unneeded data, adding capacity, or enabling pay-as-you-go for sandbox environments.

When a tenant exceeds its entitled Database, File, or Log capacity, environment creation, copy, restore, and recover operations will be restricted immediately. If the overage remains unresolved, sandbox environments that do not have pay-as-you-go billing enabled will enter Administration mode after 30 days of remaining over capacity, allowing access only to administrators. After 60 days, those sandbox environments will be disabled, preventing access for all users. Production environments are not subject to these restrictions and will remain accessible. However, environment creation, copy, restore, and recover operations will still be blocked while the tenant remains over capacity.

Deployment Timeline:
  • Rollout begins: November 9, 2026
  • Rollout completion: December 4, 2026
How does this affect me?
The Dataverse storage validation applies only to Dataverse-only tenants without Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations environment(s) or consumption. The products in-scope of storage validation include:
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Sales
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Service
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Field Service
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Voice
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Contact Center
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Project Operations (Dataverse deployments)
If your tenant exceeds its entitled storage capacity, the following lifecycle applies:

Stage Timing Impact
1. Restricted When the tenant first exceeds its entitled storage capacity, known as time zero (T0) Environment creation, copy, restore, and recover operations are blocked
2. Administration mode 30 days after the tenant first exceeds capacity - T0 Only administrators can sign in to *affected sandbox environments. All other users are blocked from accessing the environment.
3. Disabled After 60 unresolved days from T0 All users, including administrators, are blocked from *affected sandbox environments; the environment data is retained and remains available for recovery after remediation

Sandbox environments with active pay-as-you-go billing do not progress through the storage overage lifecycle. Other *affected sandbox environments in the tenant may still be affected with restrictions.

We will provide notifications that include the tenant's current storage status, the date it first exceeded capacity, its current lifecycle stage, upcoming restrictions, and recommended remediation actions.

Restrictions are removed after the tenant has returned below 100% of its entitled storage capacity. Sandbox environments with active pay-as-you-go billing are excluded from the lifecycle even if the tenant remains over storage capacity. Processing time may vary depending on the remediation method used.

What action do I need to take?
Review your environment(s) and perform the following actions before November 9, 2026:
  • Review Database, File, and Log capacity in the Power Platform admin center.
  • Remove or archive data that is no longer needed.
  • Establish data governance policies in your environment to help prevent future storage overages.
  • Purchase additional capacity or configure pay-as-you-go.
  • Inform administrators, makers, and users about the potential restrictions.
  • Review your release activities that depend on sandbox availability, and plan accordingly.
For additional information, please visit the following articles:
  • What happens when my organization exceeds storage capacity?
  • Dataverse capacity-based storage details
  • Manage data with Dataverse governance policies
  • Free up storage space
  • Add more Dataverse capacity
  • Configure pay-as-you-go in your environment
  • What environments consume tenant capacity
  • Power Platform licensing guidance
*Affected environments: Sandbox environments that do not have pay-as-you-go enabled. Any references to affected environments in this message apply exclusively to those sandbox environments.

item.title: [stayInformed] Dynamics 365 Contact Center - Let representatives set next presence to handle routing of work items
item.description:
We are announcing the ability to let customer service representatives set their next presence to handle routing of work items in Dynamics 365 Contact Center. This feature will reach general availability on October 30, 2026.

How does this affect me?
With this feature, customer service representatives can schedule a future presence status, such as Away, Do Not Disturb, or Offline, while they are still handling active customer conversations. When a customer service representative selects a new presence status, the system marks it as pending and stops assigning new conversations to them. After all active conversations and work items are completed, the system automatically updates the presence to the selected status. This setting allows customer service representatives to transition smoothly to breaks or other availability states without interrupting customer engagements or requiring manual status changes.

What action do I need to take?
This message is for awareness, and no action is required.
